contracts.problem: Renews by itself on 1 Jan at 7% more. Only 1,240 of 2,000 seats are used.
contracts.summary: This contract renews by itself on 1 Jan 2027 for ₹4.49 Cr, 7% more than today. Your team uses 1,240 of the 2,000 seats you pay for.
clauses: Clause 3.1, Fees, page 4: Customer shall pay ₹21,000 per named user per year for 2,000 named users.
Clause 12.2, Renewal, page 11: This Agreement renews automatically for successive one-year terms. Fees for each renewal term increase by seven per cent (7%).
Clause 12.3, Notice, page 11: Either party may change the number of users or terminate by written notice at least thirty (30) days before the renewal date.
contracts.missing: No clause caps the yearly rise. Typical software price rises run lower, and the seat count has never been checked since signing.
facts: Only 1,240 of 2,000 seats were used in the last 90 days. (source: Usage report from Zenvault admin console, via IT)
Asking for 1,300 seats leaves room for 5% growth. (source: Headcount plan, shared by Arjun (IT))
Similar tools renewed with a 3% rise in your last two renewals. (source: Past renewals in Sirion)
contracts.workings: Today: 2,000 seats × ₹21,000 × 1.07 = ₹4.49 Cr. Proposed: 1,300 seats × ₹21,630 (3% rise) = ₹2.81 Cr. Difference: ₹1.68 Cr a year.

contracts.item: Temporary staff for regional distribution centres
contracts.problem: Billing ₹612 an hour since July. The agreed rate card says ₹560.
contracts.summary: Since July, Prime Staffing has billed ₹612 an hour for distribution-centre staff. The rate card you agreed says ₹560. That is ₹18.2 L overcharged so far.

due.label: Before the December invoice is paid

clauses: Schedule B, Rate card, page 14: Warehouse associate (day shift): ₹560 per hour, fixed until 31 March 2027.
Clause 8.4, Invoice disputes, page 7: Customer may recover any amount invoiced above the agreed rates within twelve (12) months of the invoice date.
contracts.missing: Nothing in the contract allows a mid-year rise. The higher rate was never approved.
facts: About 7,000 hours a month are billed at ₹612. (source: Invoices in SAP S/4HANA, July to November)
No change order or approval for a new rate exists. (source: Contract history in Sirion)
contracts.workings: ₹52 an hour × about 7,000 hours a month × 5 months = ₹18.2 L.
contracts.nextAction: Claim the overcharge and fix the rate

contracts.item: Road freight, Khandala plant to western depots
contracts.problem: Diesel got cheaper, but the fuel charge on your bill didn't. The contract says it should.
contracts.summary: Diesel got cheaper, so your freight rate should have dropped 2.4%. It didn't. You have been overcharged ₹10.8 L since May.
clauses: Clause 7.2, Fuel adjustment, page 4: The freight rate shall be revised monthly. For every ₹1 per litre change in the retail diesel price in Mumbai, the rate shall change by 0.4%.
Clause 9.1, Claims, page 6: Either party may claim any amount wrongly invoiced within twelve (12) months of the invoice date.
contracts.missing: The contract already does the right thing. Nobody applied it.
facts: Diesel in Mumbai is ₹6 a litre cheaper than in April. (source: Fuel price feed)
Every invoice since May uses the April rate. (source: Freight invoices in SAP S/4HANA, matched in Sirion)
contracts.nextAction: Claim the overcharge and fix the rate

contracts.item: Housekeeping for 4 plants and the Mumbai head office
contracts.problem: Raised prices 6% in October. The contract caps rises at the inflation index, 3.4% this year.
contracts.summary: CleanCore raised prices by 6% in October. Your contract caps yearly rises at the inflation index, which is 3.4% this year.

due.label: Before the rise is locked in

clauses: Clause 5.3, Price review, page 5: Prices may be revised once a year in October. Any increase shall not exceed the change in the consumer price index for the previous twelve months.
contracts.missing: Earlier years were within the cap. This year the rise was applied without checking the index.
facts: The index named in the contract rose 3.4% in the last twelve months. (source: Inflation index feed)
Contract value is about ₹3.6 Cr a year. (source: Purchase orders in SAP Ariba)
contracts.workings: (6% − 3.4%) × ₹3.6 Cr = ₹9.4 L a year. ₹1.6 L already overpaid for October and November.
contracts.nextAction: Hold the rise to the cap

contracts.problem: Senior consultants billed at ₹1.9 L a day. The agreed rate is ₹1.6 L. Travel is also above the 10% cap.
contracts.summary: Northbridge billed 40 senior consultant days at ₹1.9 L instead of the agreed ₹1.6 L, and travel went over the 10% cap. That is ₹14 L to claim back.
clauses: Statement of work, Fees, page 3: Senior consultant: ₹1,60,000 per day. Travel and expenses are reimbursed at cost, up to 10% of fees.
contracts.missing: The higher rate matches a newer price list the firm sent by email. It was never signed.
facts: 40 senior days billed at ₹1.9 L since August. (source: Invoices in SAP S/4HANA)
Travel came to 14% of fees. (source: Expense lines on invoices)
contracts.workings: 40 days × ₹0.3 L = ₹12 L, plus ₹2 L of travel above the cap = ₹14 L.

contracts.item: Digital marketing retainer, décor and home brands
contracts.problem: Missed the agreed four campaigns a month three times this year. Service credits were never claimed.
contracts.summary: Brightline promised four campaigns a month. They delivered fewer in June, August and October. The contract gives you 10% of that month's fee back each time.

due.label: Credits must be claimed this quarter

clauses: Schedule A, Service levels, page 9: Agency will deliver four (4) campaigns per month. For any month below this level, the Agency will credit 10% of that month's retainer.
contracts.missing: Nobody tracks deliveries against the contract, so credits go unclaimed.
facts: Retainer is ₹25 L a month. (source: Invoices in SAP S/4HANA)
Delivery counts come from the agency's own monthly reports. (source: Monthly reports attached in Sirion)
